html:
A bloodless coup on 24 June 1932 that ended absolute monarchy in Siam and gave the country its first constitution.

It was carried out by the People's Party, a small group of army officers and civil servants, many of them educated in Europe. Its leaders included the lawyer Pridi Banomyong and the officer Plaek Phibunsongkhram. They were frustrated by rule by princes, and the Great Depression had hit Siam hard, forcing cuts to salaries and the army.

While King Prajadhipok was at his seaside palace, the plotters seized key princes in Bangkok and announced the end of absolute rule. The king, who had himself thought about granting a constitution, agreed to become a constitutional monarch. He later fell out with the new rulers and abdicated in 1935.

The revolution brought an elected assembly, but power soon passed to the army. Phibun became prime minister and in 1939 renamed the country Thailand. Since 1932 Thailand has seen more than a dozen coups, and the role of the monarchy remains a live question.
sum: A bloodless coup on 24 June 1932 that ended absolute monarchy in Siam and gave the country its first constitution.
